mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate component of equity discount rates, compressing the discount rate applied to future cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS declines below 4.0%, the average 20-day S&P 500 return is negative or not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 2.5% annualized inflation signals persistent price pressures, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain restrictive monetary policy and generate negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, the average 20-day S&P 500 return is positive or not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a tightening labor market, accelerating wage growth and corporate profit expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 4.0%, the average 20-day S&P 500 return is negative or not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer spending momentum, accelerating corporate revenue growth and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS increase by more than 0.5% in the prior month, the average 20-day S&P 500 return is negative or not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing output contraction (INDPRO < 105.0) signals supply chain disruptions and weak industrial activity, leading to higher inflation and Fed tightening, which generates negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 105.0, the average 60-day S&P 500 return is positive or not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong residential construction activity, serving as a leading indicator of consumer spending and economic growth, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST and 5-day S&P 500 returns is negative (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signal a rapidly tightening labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, which generates positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls in the same month, the average 20-day S&P 500 return is negative or not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), a federal funds rate increase above 4.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, which suppresses equity valuations and generates negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% and FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5%, the average 60-day S&P 500 return is positive or not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.
